# dsh-session-suite

**By heixiua** · github.com/heixiua/dsh-session-suite · MIT
· npm: `@heixui/dsh-session-suite`

Session checkpoints for DeepSeek Harness (DSH): rewind a
conversation *together with the workspace f

iles and the session memory it produced*, delete sessions for good,
share a conversation as an image

or a self-contained page — and keep a **long-term memory** that survives across
sessions and worksp

self-contained page — and keep a **long-term memory** that survives across
sessions and workspaces.
It is a DSH bundle (Host + Web Client) built against the desktop profile, and it deliberately target

s the
interaction pattern of Trae's session actions.
| Capability | Where it lives |
| Rewind to a message (conversation + files + memory) | ↺ button on every final assistant message, i

nline confirm bar above the composer |
| Delete one turn (conversation + memory only) | 🗑 button bes

ide ↺ |
| Delete a chosen run of turns | Session menu → **Delete part of the conversation**, with a

turn picker |
| Delete a session permanently | Session menu → **Delete session** (confirmation dialo

g) |
| Share a chosen range | Session menu → **Share**: pick turns, then Image / Web page / Markdown

/ JSON / copy text |
| Snapshot management | Session menu → **Session snapshots**, and Settings → *

*Session snapshots** |
| Long-term memory (global + per-workspace) | Settings → **Long-term memory**

; `【记住：…】`; the `memory` tool |
| Use WorkBuddy / Trae credits as models | **not this bundle** — see
Using WorkBuddy and Trae credits |
### What each destructive action touches
| Action | Conversation | Memory | Workspace files |

| Rewind (↺) | cut at the message | trimmed to that point | **restored** to that turn's snapshot |
|
Delete a turn (🗑) | the prompt, the reply, and the steps between them | trimmed to that point | unt

ouched |
| Delete part of the conversation | cut at the first selected turn (its prompt included) |

trimmed to that point | untouched |
| Delete session | removed from disk | removed | untouched (the

point | untouched |
| Delete session | removed from disk | removed | untouched (the folder stays) |
Only a rewind puts files back; every other delete leaves the working tree exactly as it is. A sessio

n log is
append-only, so "cut" always means "keep the prefix and retire the original" — the turns af

ter a removed range go
with it.
### What an export contains
A session log is mostly plumbing: runtime context, the skill catalog, time samples, subagent relays,

tool calls,
and the narration a model writes between tools. None of that is the conversation:
* only `source.kind === "user"` messages count as prompts — everything else in a user-role event is

dropped;
* **Final answers only** (the default) keeps your prompt plus the closing reply of each tur
ults never appear in the rich exports, and Markdown/JSON follow the same curation.
Consecutive assistant steps of one turn merge into a single card, and steps with no prose are droppe

d rather than
exported as empty `Assistant` labels.
A public share link would need a server holding the conversation; the web page file is the portable

equivalent, so
that is what this bundle produces instead of minting URLs that would only work on thi

, so
that is what this bundle produces instead of minting URLs that would only work on this machine.
## What actually gets injected

`recallLimit` is a ceiling, not a quota. Filling it on every turn is how a weak
question drags six u

nrelated memories into the prompt and then asserts they are
relevant. The injected count steps down

with the evidence — the full budget for a
strong match, fewer for a weaker one, and one entry when t

he question barely
matches anything. A question that matches nothing injects nothing.

A small resident layer runs alongside: the two most important memories ride along
regardless of the

question. Without it, an ordinary follow-up like 「继续」 shares
no vocabulary with anything, a strict r

elevance filter would inject nothing at
all, and the feature would look broken rather than selective

. Set
`residentLimit: 0` to turn it off.

Every candidate that is *not* injected is reported with the rule that dropped it
(`no-match` or `cap

acity`). A memory system that silently decides not to recall
something is indistinguishable from one

that has forgotten it; naming the reason
is the difference between a black box and a debuggable fea

has forgotten it; naming the reason
is the difference between a black box and a debuggable feature.

The memory settings page has a **"What would this question recall?"** box that
shows this live: type

a question, see which memories it pulls in, how many the
evidence justifies, and why each of the re

st was left out. The dry run is
read-only (`touch: false`), so trying queries cannot re-rank your ow

t out. The dry run is
read-only (`touch: false`), so trying queries cannot re-rank your own library.
## What changed in 0.10.1

Five fixes for defects 0.10.0 shipped with, all found by auditing the release
against the live libra
ry rather than by reading the code.
| Area | Before | Now |
| Cross-store contradictions | The scan ran inside the per-store loop, so a global rule and a worksp
ace rule that contradict each other were **both injected into every prompt and never queued** (measu
red: 0.737 similarity, both scopes injected, queue empty) | The scan also compares the global store

against each workspace store; settling writes the loser back to whichever store it lives in |
| Conf
lict queue reads | `conflicts(cwd)` filtered the shared queue file by workspace and wrote the filter
ed array back, so **"not mine" became "stale"** — opening the memory page in one workspace deleted e
very other workspace's pending conflicts (measured: 1 → 0) | Only items a call actually inspected ar

e pruned; other workspaces' items are written back untouched |
| Lessons quoting a credential | A fa
ilure message echoing `sk-…` marked the whole distilled lesson `secret`, and a secret is never injec
ted — the mistake became invisible while the credential stayed in the library | Credentials are reda

cted at capture (`[已脱敏]`) and the lesson stays injectable |
| Lessons with no resolvable workspace |
`remember({scope:'workspace'})` throws without a `cwd`; the hook caught and logged it, silently dro
pping the lesson | Falls back to the global store, which is where a lesson that applies anywhere bel

n | Falls back to the global store, which is where a lesson that applies anywhere belongs |
